vulnerability.title: Jenkins stores build authorization tokens unencrypted in job config.xml files

fixed_releases.verified_content: The 2.541 release commit ea9c7278 has the SECURITY-783 commit 4710d653 as an ancestor (git merge-base --is-ancestor exits 0), and BuildAuthorizationToken.java at the tag is blob 96fb27f8, the same blob as at 4710d653. The 2.528.3 release commit 40e29179 has the LTS commit c3d776a4 as an ancestor, and the file at that tag is blob e6d7de58, the same blob as at c3d776a4. In both fixed trees the token field is a hudson.util.Secret and the XStream converter writes Secret.getEncryptedValue(), so new and migrated job configurations contain the token only in encrypted form. BuildAuthorizationTokenMigrationTest loads a job whose config.xml holds a plain <authToken> and asserts it is migrated to an encrypted Secret on save and that the plaintext no longer appears.

severity.numeric_level_rationale: NVD publishes a single CVSS 3.1 metric, 4.3 MEDIUM, from the Secondary source (CISA-ADP); there is no Primary metric. OSV/GHSA repeats the same 4.3 vector and records MODERATE, which is the same medium band. The CNA container has no CVSS metric. Every published severity level is medium, so the level is consistent and the score is not averaged.

vulnerability.category_l2: The build authorization token is held in a plain String and emitted verbatim by the XStream single-value converter, so job config.xml stores it in clear text and the config.xml redaction layer, which handles Secret values only, does not mask it

description: A Jenkins job can be triggered remotely with a build authorization token, captured on the job configuration form (pseudoRemoteTrigger / authToken) and stored on the job as a BuildAuthorizationToken. At 2.441 that class keeps the value in a plain String field (line 49) and its XStream ConverterImpl serializes it with ((BuildAuthorizationToken) obj).token (lines 109-112), so every job config.xml on the controller contains the build authorization token in clear text. Two consequences follow from the same storage decision. First, any user who can read job configuration XML - in particular Item/Extended Read, which is served through the config.xml endpoint - obtains the plaintext token, because the config.xml redaction introduced in 2.500 only knows how to mask Secret values and BuildAuthorizationToken is not one. Second, anyone with access to the controller file system can read the token directly from the file. The 2.541/2.528.3 fix commits 4710d653 and c3d776a4 change the field to hudson.util.Secret, keep a String constructor that marks the value as originally plaintext, make the converter write Secret.getEncryptedValue() and set fromPlaintext=false when re-saving, accept both plaintext and already-encrypted values when loading old XML, and add an ItemListener that reports legacy plaintext tokens through OldDataMonitor. BuildAuthorizationTokenMigrationTest loads a job config that contains <authToken> with the plaintext OLDTOKEN and asserts the token is migrated, the re-saved config no longer contains the plaintext and contains the encrypted value instead, and the OldData administrative monitor reports the affected job only.

critical_operation.description: The token is a plain String and the converter's toString returns it verbatim, so the value written into job config.xml is cleartext. Because it is not a Secret, the 2.500 config.xml redaction cannot mask it, which is what makes the token readable by Item/Extended Read users as well as from the controller file system.

entry_point.description: Reading a job's config.xml (GET /job/<name>/config.xml) as a user with Overall/Read and Item/Extended Read but without Item/Configure, or reading the same file on the controller file system.

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA, NVD, OSV and the GitHub advisory agree on the mechanism (build authorization tokens stored unencrypted in job config.xml, readable by Item/Extended Read or from the file system) and on the fixed releases (2.541 weekly, 2.528.3 LTS). NVD publishes no Primary metric; its only metric is the CISA-ADP Secondary 4.3 MEDIUM, which OSV/GHSA repeats as 4.3 MODERATE, and the CNA has no metric, so all published levels are medium. CWE-312 is recorded by NVD's Secondary source and by GHSA; the CNA lists none. The GHSA ECOSYSTEM weekly range introduced=2.529 conflicts with the CNA text and the CVE GIT range (introduced 0); this dataset follows the CNA and GIT range and records the conflict. CVE-2025-67638 covers the unmasked display of the same token on the configuration form; the two are separate advisory rows even though one commit fixes both, and this dossier claims only the cleartext storage.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read BuildAuthorizationToken at 2.441 and confirm the token is a plain String and the converter writes it verbatim into config.xml.
An independent reviewer must confirm the fix commits 4710d653/c3d776a4 switch the field to Secret with an encrypted converter and are contained in releases 2.541 and 2.528.3.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range (weekly <=2.540, LTS <=2.528.2) and that 2.441 is inside it.
An independent reviewer must confirm all published severity levels are medium (4.3) and record CWE-312.
An independent reviewer must confirm this entry is distinct from CVE-2025-67638 and from the other Jenkins CVEs in the dataset.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Static verification only; no Jenkins instance, HTTP request or test was run.

The mechanism by which a config.xml reader obtains the plaintext is the XStream serialization of the job, not a dedicated endpoint; the config.xml redaction added in 2.500 masks Secret values only and therefore does not cover this field, which the fix's own migration test demonstrates by expecting the plaintext before migration.
The fix also masks the value on the configuration form; that display aspect is CVE-2025-67638 and is outside this row.
The LTS fix commit c3d776a4 has no visible parent in the shallow mirror, so its parent relationship was not checked; its containment in the 2.528.3 release commit was checked directly.
The GHSA ECOSYSTEM weekly range introduced=2.529 conflicts with the CNA and the CVE GIT range; the conflict is documented, not resolved silently.
open_questions: Whether older job configurations created before the token feature existed are equally affected was not enumerated; the migration test covers the plaintext-token case.
